FOREWORD This Indian Standard was adopted by the Bureau of Indian Standards, after the draft finalized by the Paper and Its Products (Excluding Packaging Materials) Sectional Committee had been approved by the Chemical Division Council. Post card is the cheapest mode of communication available in India. Department of Post, Government of India wanted to build the quality in the post card not only for its performance but also for its ability to withstand the various mechanical stresses it undergoes during the transit. There is no 1S0 Standard on the subject. This standard has been prepared based on indigenous manufacturer's data/practices prevalent in the field in India. This standard also complements the efforts made by the Department of Post (DoP), Government of India for speedy delivery of public mail. While formulating the standard due considerations are given with respect to the requirements of DoP and the recommendations of Universal Postal Union (UPU). The composition of the Committee responsible for formulation of this standard is given in Annex A,

For the purpose of deciding whether a particular requirement of this standard is complied with, the final value, observed or calculated, expressing the result of a test or analysis, shall be rounded off in accordance with IS 2: 1960 `Rules for rounding off numerical values (revised)'. The number of significant places retained in the rounded off value should be the same as that of the specified value in this standard.

Indian Standard POST CARD -- SPECIFICATION
1 SCOPE This standard prescribes the requirements and methods of sampling and test for post card intended for general purpose only and not for commercial. 2 REFERENCES The standards listed below contain provisions which through reference in this text, constitute provisions of this standard. At the time of publication, the editions indicated were valid. All standards are subject to revisions, and parties to agreements based on this standard are encouraged to investigate the possibility of applying the most recent editions of the standards indicated below. 4.2 Grammage Nominal grammage of pulp board shall be 205g/m2. When tested according to 6 of IS 1060 (Part 1), no single test result shall vary by more than + 6 percent from the nominal grammage. Further, the mean of 10 test results shall not vary from the nominal grammage by more than* 4 percent. 4.3 Thickness Thickness of pulp board shall be in between 0.22 mm and 0.25 mm, when tested according to 7 of IS 1060 (Part 1). 4.4 The pulp board shall also comply requirements given in Table 1. 4.1.1 The material shall be of buff pulp board, machine finished and machine calendered manufactured from 100 percent chemical pulp of straw, bagasse and/or wood. 4.1.2 The pulp board shall have a smooth, even surface on both sides and shall be suitable for writing in ink and good class letter printing. 4.1.3 The pulp board shall be uniform in thickness, free from blemishes, specks, holes, undigested lumps and chips and as far as possible free from fluff and dust. 4.1.4 Shade of the pulp board shall be as agreed to between the purchaser and supplier. 1

4.5 The reels shall be accurately slit and wound with even tension on strong straw board centres of 125 mm internal diameter. The straw board centres are to be plugged with suitable seasoned wooden plugs of sufficient length to prevent damage by crushing. 4.6 Joints in the reel are to be as few as possible but not more than 4 in a reel. It shall be as neat as possible so as to pass through the machine smoothly. 4.7 Butt joint shall be joined with cellophane tape. The joints shall be indicated by red arrow well in advance so that in case the joints are thick, the joints can be passed through the machine by reducing the speed and pressure on the machine to prevent machine damage.

IS 15307:2003 5 REQUIREMENTS 5.1 General 5.1.1 Post card shall be a flat, generally rectangular in shape and made from one sheet of paper. No part of a post card which is laid on a flat surface shall protrude more than 8 mm from the surface. 5.1.2 Post card shall be free from tears, dog-ears and perforation type of defects. 5.2 Sizes Post card shall be of 90 mm x 140 mm in size. A tolerance of+ 2 mm shall be permitted on sizes. 5.3 At the lowest part of the address side of the post card, 20 mm wide covering the whole length of the card shall be reserved for bar coding. 5.4 Printing The post cards, may be suitably and distinctly printed as agreed to between the purchaser and the supplier. 6 PACKING 6.1 Packing Post card shall be securely packed as agreed to between the purchaser and the supplier. 6.2 Marking Each package information: a) b) c) d) e) f) shall be marked with the following

All the packages of post cards belonging to the same batch of manufacture shall be grouped together to constitute a lot. Each lot shall be tested separately for various requirements of the specifications. 7.2 General Requirement for Sampling

7.2.1 Samples shall be protected from exposure to heat, direct sunlight, liquids, varying humidity conditions as well as any other harmful influences. 7.2.2 Samples shall be handled as little as possible and contact with sweated hands shall be strictly avoided. 7.3 The number of post cards to be sampled from each lot shall be as given in Table 2. The samples shall be drawn by the method of random selection as per IS 4905. Table 2 Scale of Sampling

Marking 7,4 Tests for checking the requirements of pulp board for post cards as per Table 1 shall be conducted per 10000 post cards or part thereof. 7.5 Criteria for Conformity a) While conducting the tests for paper quality, no failure shall occur for the lot to be accepted as conforming to the specification. A post card shall be termed as defective if it fails in one or more visual or dimensional requirements as per 5.1 to 5.4. The number of defective in the sample shall be less than or equal to the permissible number of defective (acceptance number as per COI3 of Table 2) for the lot to be accepted as conforming to this specification.

6.2.1 BIS Certification

The product may also be marked with the Standard Mark. b) 6.2.2 The use of the Standard Mark is governed by the provisions of the Bureau of Indian Standards Act, 1986 and the Rules and Regulations made thereunder. The details of conditions under which the licence for the use of the Standard Mark may be granted to manufacturers or producers maybe obtained from the Bureau of Indian Standards.
